merger_description:
The transaction concerns the proposed acquisition of all shares in and sole control over United Initiators Holding GmbH, United Initiators GmbH and Bayern Acquisition LLC and each of their direct and indirect subsidiaries (collectively, **United Initiators**) by Unna BidCo GmbH (the **Acquisition**). Unna BidCo GmbH is a newly formed special purpose vehicle indirectly controlled by Triton Fund 6 GP SARL in its capacity as general partner of Triton Fund 6 SCSp (which, together with a number of other limited partnerships, form part of **Triton Fund 6**).

Triton Fund 6 is one of several investment funds (the **Triton Funds**) managed and advised by entities being part of the Triton group (collectively, **Triton**). The Triton Funds, including Triton Fund 6, are dedicated to investing in medium-sized companies headquartered in Central and Northern Europe, with a particular focus on three core sectors: Industrial Tech, Business Services, and Healthcare.

United Initiators is a global manufacturer of active oxygen chemicals used as initiators in the polymerisation process. Specifically, United Initiators manufactures and supplies (i) organic peroxides, (ii) persulfates, and (iii) hydrogen peroxide. United Initiators also supplies a limited range of accelerators and inhibitors used in the curing of unsaturated polyester resins. United Initiators is headquartered in Pullach, Germany, and operates several manufacturing sites globally.

United Initiators’ products are used by customers across the polymer industry, serving a range of end uses, including consumer goods, housing and infrastructure, transportation, sustainable technologies, textile and paper, and health and cosmetics.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Triton (or its
connected entities) and United Initiators in Australia
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
